current_evidence: Newham's 'Planning permission application process' page links this 'Planning Application Requirements (PAR)' PDF as its requirements document, the PDF is dated December 2024 in its text, and a web search found no newer version.

issues.detail: Almost every tab_item is submission or process text, not a validation requirement: the 10MB attachment limit, splitting large documents into parts, CDs or paper copies for the largest schemes, emailing BACS remittance advice to cash.control@ and planning.validation@, 'please email planning.validation@newham.gov.uk', hard copies at validation, the £60 admin fee for direct submission, 'the evidence and reasons provided will be reviewed by the Validation Team', Argus format and publishing notes for viability, and the fragments 'Strategic Access Management and Monitoring Strategy (SAMMS) Standalone Policy Requirements Local Local Plan (2018):' and 'Within this form you will be required to stipulate what option you are relying on for payment of the SAMMS contribution.'
issues.evidence: PAR Dec 2024, 'How to Submit' / 'Preferred Method of Payment': direct submissions 'will incur an administration fee of £60'; 'The maximum file size of any single attachment is 10mb'

issues.detail: Heritage / Character / Place-making Asset Statement is not captured. Trigger: Listed Building Consent; works to listed, locally listed or identified non-designated heritage assets; ground disturbance in Archaeological Priority Areas or significant ground disturbance elsewhere; applications in or next to Conservation Areas. This applies to householder and LBC applications, which the workbook shows with no heritage item (LBC is '(none)').
issues.evidence: PAR: 'Planning applications in Conservation Areas or adjacent to them' (Heritage/Character/Place-making Asset Statement)

issues.detail: Airport Safeguarding Information (London City Airport) is not captured as a requirement. Its trigger is every application and prior approval. Its content bullets (external lighting, bird attractors, cranes, people in the Public Safety Zone) were instead used as the trigger for 'Lighting Assessment'.
issues.evidence: PAR, Airport Safeguarding Information: 'All applications and prior approvals'

issues.detail: Housing statements are missing: Housing Quality Statement (all new housing, plus play space information where 10 or more children are expected); Family Housing Statement (housing sites with capacity for 10+ units, FUL/OUT/COU/REM); Affordable Housing Statement (housing sites with capacity for 10+ units, and all student housing); Specialist Housing Statement (non-conventional housing such as hostels, student accommodation and C2 care). Fragments of these triggers appear only inside Grokbot's 'Open space / play space assessment' row.
issues.evidence: PAR local list: 'Applications for housing on sites with the capacity for 10 or more residential units (includes FUL/OUT/COU/REM applications)'

issues.detail: Economic and employment requirements are missing: Infrastructure Sufficiency Statement (all major development); Economic Development Statement (applications proposing employment-generating floorspace); Employment Strategy (all major development); Managed Release / Transition Statement (release of SIL/industrial land under Policy J2, or loss of employment floorspace in LMUAs, non-released LILs/SILs, or non-designated employment sites over 0.1ha or 1,000 sq m). The Managed Release text appears only as the wrong trigger for 'Planning Statement'.
issues.evidence: PAR: 'Managed Release/Transition Statement - Within the Planning Statement, cross-referencing Employment Strategy as necessary'

issues.detail: Town centre and community use requirements are missing: Community Facilities Statement (creation, intensification or loss of community facilities such as education, healthcare, leisure, places of worship, pubs, public toilets); Town Centre Sequential Test (main town centre uses outside existing centres or Strategic Site allocations); Retail / Leisure Impact Assessment (retail over 300 sq m or leisure over 2,500 sq m outside centres where not in accordance with the Development Plan).
issues.evidence: PAR local list, Community Facilities Statement / Town Centre Sequential Test / Retail-Leisure Impact Assessment rows

issues.detail: Environmental requirements are missing: Health Impact Assessment (all major residential and mixed-use proposals); Cumulative Impact Statement (development in an identified cumulative impact zone); Surface Water Drainage Strategy with the LLFA pro-forma (all major, any application needing an FRA, any development in a Critical Drainage Area); Pollution Management Statement covering air quality (all development), noise, ventilation/extraction, land contamination, radiation and interference; Demolition Method Statement (Prior Notification of Proposed Demolition, and most majors with significant demolition). Grokbot has 'Ventilation / Extraction' only.
issues.evidence: PAR: Health Impact Assessment - 'All major residential developments and mixed use proposals'; Demolition Method Statement - 'Prior Notification of Proposed Demolition applications'

issues.detail: Statement of Community Involvement / Consultation Statement (all FUL, OUT, REM and COU applications) and Parking & Service Details (COU and FUL unless parking or servicing is unaffected) are not captured as requirements. SCI text appears only inside the mislabelled 'Schedule of works (listed building)' row, and parking appears only as the fragment 'and proposed cycle parking.'.
issues.evidence: PAR: Statement of Community Involvement - 'All FUL , OUT, REM and COU applications'

issues.detail: The Flood Risk Assessment is placed under Householder because the word 'householder' appears in its text, but that text is an exemption. The PAR does not require an FRA in Flood Zones 2/3 for householder development.
issues.evidence: PAR, Flood Risk Assessment: required in Flood Zone 2 or 3 'unless the development is a householder'

issues.detail: About 25 items carry the note 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', even though the PAR names the application types for many of them, and several types are wrongly marked '(none)'. Examples: Planning Statement and SCI apply to FUL, OUT, REM and COU, yet Reserved matters is '(none)' and Outline lacks them. The Heritage Statement applies to Listed Building Consent, which is '(none)'. Airport Safeguarding and SAMMS apply to prior approvals, which are '(none)'. The Demolition Method Statement applies to prior notification of demolition. EIA 'may apply to REM and discharge of conditions'.
issues.evidence: PAR: Planning Statement - 'All FUL, OUT, REM and COU applications'; SAMMS - 'applications for planning permission and prior approval applications'

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts are policy-reference lists or fragments, not the PAR's 'when required' text. CIL is given policy references only (actual: new buildings or extensions of 100 sq m+ GIA, or any new dwelling). EIA is given policy references (actual: EIA Regulations Schedule 1/2 development). Fire Statement is given policy references (actual: all majors plus Planning Gateway One schemes). Viability is given 'appraisals will be published without redaction' (actual: below-policy affordable/family housing, or non-residential 500 sq m+ with non-compliant BREEAM). Energy is given a carbon off-setting note (actual: SC1/SC2 thresholds). Tall buildings is given 'scale of tall buildings and ... hierarchy' (actual: over 6 storeys or 17.05m). Other fragments: 'of the SAMMS contribution.', 'and proposed cycle parking.', 'way of pre-application advice.', 'a pre-existing block plan will be required.'.
issues.evidence: PAR, Tall Buildings Study: 'in excess of 6 storeys or 17.05 metres above ground level'

issues.detail: Several rows carry text from a different requirement. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' contains BS5837 tree text and the start of the SCI; the PAR has no such requirement. 'Lighting Assessment' uses the airport safeguarding bullets (actual trigger: any proposal, including changes to open space, that includes or makes necessary external lighting). 'Travel Plan' reuses the Transport Statement text (actual: all majors, sites in or next to a Sustainable Transport Opportunity Area or Congestion Zone, F1 and E(e)/E(f) uses, and minors with significant transport implications). 'Planning Statement' uses the Managed Release text. 'Arboricultural' should follow the Landscaping Statement trigger (outdoor space in the red line, or works near mature or TPO trees).
issues.evidence: PAR, Lighting Assessment: 'All proposals (including changes to open space) that include or make necessary external lighting.'

issues.detail: The Design and Access Statement trigger suggests a DAS is needed 'irrespective of scheme size'. The PAR's trigger is all major development (except material change of use, waste, engineering or mining), plus schemes in designated areas that create a dwelling or 100 sq m+ of non-residential floorspace. The Sustainability Statement trigger (major residential; non-residential 500 sq m+) is also missing from the merged 'Energy / Sustainability Statement' row.
issues.evidence: PAR, DAS: 'All major development (except a material change of use, waste development, engineering or mining operations)'
issues.grok_comment: The workbook DAS trigger omits the 'Applies to' column (all major development except change of use/waste/mining; designated areas with 1+ dwelling or 100 sq m+). But 'irrespective of scheme size' isn't a Grokbot distortion: it is the PAR's own DAS wording ('it is considered necessary ... irrespective of scheme size').
issues.claude_response: Partly accepted. "Irrespective of scheme size" is the council's own wording; the missing "applies to" thresholds stand.

summary: Grokbot's link is the current Newham PAR (December 2024). The capture is poor: tab_items are almost all submission and process text, about 20 local requirements are missing (Heritage Statement, Airport Safeguarding, housing statements, HIA, SWDS, Pollution, SCI and others), many triggers are fragments or text from the wrong requirement, and application types are guessed even where the PAR names them.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
